Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:12:00 +02:00
Subject: EU GDPR: DPA & SCCs — execution plan for Order Form amendments

Sophie / Steve — thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, attaching: Redwood_DPA_v3_redline.docx and a first-pass OrderForm_Amendment_Draft.pdf that folds in the agreed scope and retention terms. High level asks from our side: 

- Confirm whether you will sign Redwood's DPA (processor append) or insist on Orchid's MSA-first approach. We can support either but need one signed before provisioning EU-dedicated capacity.
- SCCs: we propose using the standard EU Commission Module 2 (Controller-Processor) and Module 3 where applicable; suggest applying the recent EDPB clarifications — see redline comments.
- Subprocessors: we will accept the limited subprocessor list approach with 30-day notice for additions (our standard).
- Transfer impact: we flagged a short Transfer Impact Addendum (TIA) clause in the DPA; please confirm whether your privacy team needs a fuller assessment.

Target timeline: DPA redline exchange today — final sign-off by EOD Thursday (21 May) to keep the FY Q3 onboarding window. If Orchid prefers, we can sign the DPA/OrderForm via DocuSign and then follow with the MSA redlines.

Next steps I propose:
1) Sophie: can you consolidate a single PDF with your material redlines and send back by EOD today?
2) Karthik & Laura: internal alignment on negotiation boundaries (I cc'd you).
3) Diego: security will respond to the flagged questionnaire items by tomorrow.

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_v3_redline.docx (redline), OrderForm_Amendment_Draft.pdf

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Director, Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com
+1 415 555 0182

Note: Redwood is open to document-by-document flexibility for enterprise accounts; anything materially different from our standard roles/clauses will need Legal sign-off.

- We prefer to have the DPA incorporated by reference into the MSA and executed together, but we can execute the DPA separately if Redwood requires earlier capacity. Will confirm final preference by EOD.
- SCCs: our privacy lead prefers Module 1 (Controller only) for our data flows where we act as controller; for any Processor relationships we will need Module 2. I will mark these in our redline PDF.

Team — quick internal note on negotiation posture and acceptable fallbacks.

1) Roles: Redwood will accept Processor role language where we only process customer data under documented instructions (keep our standard Processor warranties). If Orchid insists on Controller-Controller language for jointly-determined features, escalate to Legal.
2) SCCs: we should aim to adopt the Commission's standard Controller-Processor clauses where Orchid operates as controller. For cross-border processing where Redwood uses US-based telemetry or logging, include the TIA and the supplemental safeguards we proposed (encryption at rest + limited access logging).
3) Subprocessors: no open-ended consent. 30-day notification with the right to object for specific categories (e.g., analytics) — our standard.
4) Liability/indemnities: push to keep limits consistent with the Order Form (cap = contracted fees x12) — finance will confirm.

I ran a quick read with Security: see attached security-questionnaire-answers.pdf for the answers they requested from Orchid; Diego, please add anything missing.

If Orchid pushes for MSA-first, we can agree to a two-step signature (DPA + Order Form now; MSA after) but only if Procurement confirms the PO number and payment terms.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales, EMEA — Redwood Inference
